name: Absent Radius-Anogenital Anomalies Syndrome
aliases: Absent Radius with Anogenital Anomalies Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Absent Radius-Anogenital Anomalies Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Congenital bilateral or unilateral absence of the radius bone
Presence of anogenital anomalies such as hypospadias, ambiguous genitalia, or anal atresia
Additional upper limb anomalies including hypoplastic or absent thumbs

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent radius (unilateral or bilateral) plus at least one anogenital anomaly
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by radiographic imaging; genetic testing may assist but no specific gene identified.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; occasional anemia
imaging: Radiographs showing absent or hypoplastic radius
Ultrasound or MRI for renal and cardiac anomalies
genetic: No definitive gene mutation identified; possible sporadic or multifactorial inheritance
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic limb and anogenital anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Limb anomalies less specific to radius absence

redFlags: Bilateral absent radius with severe anogenital malformations
Feeding intolerance or failure to thrive due to anorectal anomalies
Presence of cardiac or renal malformations requiring urgent intervention
references: Rosenberg HK et al. Congenital absence of the radius with anogenital anomalies: a distinct syndrome. Am J Med Genet. 1990.
Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) - Entry not assigned
